category: http tunnel over a wireguard link issued by curl

free_tier.stated: SSL-terminated HTTP tunnels to your local machine - no custom software required, thanks to Wireguard

egress.terms: No allowance or price is published; the page is four lines long.; ingress: http-only

chaining: Carries HTTP only; the WG link is the transport, not the ingress.
binding_note: Nothing is published, so the byte wall is unknown, and the service is a hobby endpoint whose capacity is one host. Ingress is HTTPS only, so no UDP and no raw TCP reaches a user: the WireGuard link is how the vendor carries the HTTP tunnel, not a port a user can serve on.

identity_cost.detail: no account: the curl request is the whole signup.

reliability_note: One community host with no stated capacity or SLA.
confidence_note: The page sets no quota, so only a live transfer shows the real tolerance; the risk is that a shared community endpoint disappears.

evidence.proved: 'curl https://tunnel.pyjam.as/8080 > tunnel.conf && wg-quick up ./tunnel.conf'; 'You can now access ... on https://<unique_slug>.tunnel.pyjam.as/'

notes: The most interesting no-account entry in the sweep: a WireGuard config with zero registration, but the far side terminates HTTPS so the WireGuard link carries only HTTP. The same request shape would not forward a raw UDP port.

extras.wg_detail: The registration endpoint is the URL itself: 'curl https://tunnel.pyjam.as/8080 > tunnel.conf && wg-quick up ./tunnel.conf'. The port in the path is the local service, and the response is a wg-quick config.
extras.volume_stated: No allowance or price is published; the page is four lines long.
